tagline: A hundred and five miles of Blue Ridge crest, at thirty-five.
intro: Outside Front Royal the drive leaves US 340, passes the entrance station and winds up into the Blue Ridge. From there it keeps to the crest all the way to Rockfish Gap, where the Blue Ridge Parkway takes over. Cement mileposts on the west side count off the miles from 0 to 105, the limit is 35, and the Appalachian Trail follows close by for most of the way.

Herbert Hoover, who kept a fishing camp on the Rapidan, called for the road, and the first section opened in 1934. One resort was there before any of it. The road passes through a tunnel under Marys Rock and reaches its high point, 3,680 feet, at Skyland.

moments.title: Skyland
moments.text: Built in 1895 as Stony Man Camp and once advertised as a dude ranch, it was kept and enlarged by the park when most older buildings were cleared away.

moments.title: Hawksbill Mountain
moments.text: A short hike from Upper Hawksbill parking climbs to a stone platform on the park's highest summit, 4,050 feet, where balsam fir grows as though it were in northern New England.

moments.title: Big Meadows
moments.text: Roosevelt dedicated the park and the drive here in 1935. Each lodge room keeps a stone fireplace and a supply of firewood, though gas does the heating.

practical: Marys Rock Tunnel at mile 32.2 has a clearance of 12 feet 8 inches. The drive closes from dusk to dawn from November to early January and may close after snow or ice, and an entrance fee is charged.
